1 compensation in terms of orders (Annexure P/1 and P/9).
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that acquisition proceedings for acquisition part of his land in Survey No.6 were undertaken and award was passed vide order dated 08.11.2017 (Annexure P/1).

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that initially the alignment of the canal to be constructed was from a different place in his land in Survey No.6, but thereafter the alignment was changed to a different place in the same survey number.
Learned counsel submits that due to change in alignment, various trees planted by the petitioner were destroyed by the respondent.
These trees were coming in way of changed alignment of the canal.

Learned counsel further refers to the report of Sub Divisional Officer (Annexure P/7) dated 22.11.2017, which shows that certain trees in various survey numbers including Survey No.6 have been destroyed in course of construction of canal.
A direction is sought for compensation for destruction of such trees.
Learned counsel submits that while passing award (Annexure P/1), the damage for destruction of such trees was assessed, but it has not been paid.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State submits that the land acquisition proceedings could not be completed within the statutory period as per Section 19 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, the proceedings stood lapse and declaration to this effect was also published.

Thus, it is stated by State that since the acquisition proceedings have lapsed, the award (Annexure P/1) does not survive and no money can be paid to the petitioner as per the assessment made by such award.
Upon considering rival submissions of the parties, it is clear that the acquisition proceedings have lapsed as they have not completed within the stipulated period.
As the acquisition proceedings have lapsed, award has also lost its force.
However, the State admits in various documents that trees of the petitioner have already been destroyed while constructing the canal.
It is not the case where compensation has been assessed for anticipated destruction of trees.
It is a case where destruction of trees has already taken place.
However, the actual number of trees so destroyed is not on record and the quantum as being claimed by the petitioner for destruction of trees cannot be accepted.

As the destruction of trees for a project initiated by the State, which seems to have been later on abandoned by the State, is clear from the record, the petitioner has made out a case for grant of compensation for the trees destroyed in execution of that project.
Consequently, this petition is allowed and the petitioner is held entitled for being compensated with price of the trees destroyed while constructing the canal.
The Collector/respondent No.2 is directed to look into the matter and ascertain the number of trees destroyed while executing the now abandoned project of construction of canal.
The Collector would ascertain the appropriate cost of the trees and ensure payment of the same to the petitioner.
Let this exercise be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Certified copy as per rules.
